reject --option=value and every other semantic duplicate form before evaluator import
add an external exact-SHA root for the intended M312 contract and launcher pair
force result_dir and per_frame.csv to one empty canonical result root
strictly validate nested receipt identity, ordered rows, finite AEE and all admission fields
generate and self-verify an exact four-entry manifest plus seal
required_before_m313: complete all M312 repairs and seal one real baseline
generate a new M313 contract exact-binding baseline receipt/profile/per-frame/launch/manifest/seal and M309 selection freeze

duplicate_argument_attack.method: Imported only each launcher's unique_option helper and reproduced the generic wrapper argparse option surface; evaluator and launcher main were never invoked.

dual_result_root_exploit.chain: The outer launcher records the first --path-results value. A later --path-results=SECOND is accepted by the generic wrapper. The evaluator writes SECOND, while the outer launcher can inspect and seal pre-existing artifacts under FIRST.
dual_result_root_exploit.impact: A forged baseline or candidate root can be sealed independently of the GPU execution, including altered admission fields.

m312.impact: A clone can preserve current launcher/wrapper/module hashes while rebinding config, checkpoint, inputs, promotion gate or claims. Self-authentication is not a root of trust.

m313.impact: The six baseline SHA bindings are only as trustworthy as the as-yet-unrooted future candidate contract.

manifest_path_and_replacement_audit.assessment: Exact individual SHA checks are useful, but they do not make the manifest meaningful or close contract-root substitution.

json_and_aee_trust_boundary.risk: Different decimal strings can collapse to the same binary float, and overflowed finite JSON syntax can become infinity. A forged dual-root artifact can exploit the permissive post-run parser.
json_and_aee_trust_boundary.required: Use duplicate-key rejecting JSON, Decimal parsed from canonical strings, explicit finite checks and independent delta/gate recomputation.

baseline_receipt_admission_semantics.assessment_of_contract_claim: premature; it should express intended scope or remain false until the sealed launch receipt exists
baseline_receipt_admission_semantics.note: modified_network_forward=true in the generic receipt denotes the installed evaluation wrapper, not a lossy tau0 accuracy claim; the dedicated launch receipt must state this explicitly.

findings.title: Semantic duplicate arguments still bypass both dedicated launchers
findings.evidence: Exact-token duplicates are rejected, but --option=value is not counted by unique_option. The generic argparse wrapper then uses the later value for 10 recognized options. The path-results variant creates separate execution and sealing roots.
findings.impact: M310's first P0 remains open. A full GPU execution can use different contract/config/checkpoint/tau/sample/BN/baseline or output roots than the outer launcher audited, and a prebuilt first root can be sealed.
findings.required_fix: Parse once with allow_abbrev=false, reject every repeated destination regardless of syntax, never forward raw sys.argv, and construct a fresh canonical wrapper argv.

findings.title: The contract authenticates the launcher, but nothing authenticates the intended contract
findings.evidence: M312 and M313 accept any JSON with the expected schema/milestone that repeats the live launcher/wrapper/module hashes. Neither launcher contains nor receives a separately sealed expected contract SHA.
findings.impact: A clone contract can rebind the checkpoint, config, inputs, baseline and gate while passing the current self-referential identity checks.
findings.required_fix: Add a separately sealed runner/launch manifest that exact-pins both launcher and intended contract, and verify that root before importing the generic wrapper.

findings.title: M313 has no post-baseline candidate contract to review or trust
findings.evidence: No M313 contract exists. The source anticipates six exact baseline bindings, but their paths and hashes cannot exist until a repaired M312 baseline is complete.
findings.impact: M310's arbitrary-baseline P0 is directionally addressed but not closed for execution; M313 must not start from a hand-built or cloned contract.
findings.required_fix: After a repaired M312 run, generate the exact-SHA M313 contract, seal its launch root, and submit both for a new independent review.

findings.title: Baseline manifests are sealed as bytes but not validated as artifact maps
findings.evidence: M312 records path.name even if per_frame is outside result_dir and never replays the manifest. M313 checks the seal hash but not its filename token or any manifest entry.
findings.impact: A sealed manifest can be non-replayable, omit or misname the baseline artifacts, or disagree with the individually bound files.
findings.required_fix: Force canonical co-located names, reject duplicate/path-escape entries, require exactly four expected hashes, verify the seal filename and replay the manifest before success.

findings.title: Nested baseline and candidate identities are incomplete
findings.evidence: M312 does not compare receipt contract/config/checkpoint/wrapper/module/evaluator/docs identities or receipt order against CSV. M313 does not validate the baseline launch's contract/runtime/tau/BN fields and does not validate candidate receipt nested identity or independently recompute its AEE gate.
findings.impact: Path-root substitution or forged artifacts can satisfy the shallow checks while describing a different run.
findings.required_fix: Bind and compare every nested identity and ordered row, then independently recompute AEE and admission from the sealed profiles/CSV.

findings.title: Security JSON and AEE comparisons remain permissive
findings.evidence: Both launchers use plain json.loads; M313 compares AEE through binary float equality without finite or exact-decimal checks.
findings.impact: Duplicate keys, overflow-to-infinity and decimal aliasing weaken the trust boundary, especially under the dual-root attack.
findings.required_fix: Use strict duplicate-key parsing, reject nonfinite/overflowed numbers, compare canonical Decimal values, and recompute delta <= 0.02.

findings.title: Baseline admission language and checks are not fully fail-closed
findings.evidence: The pre-run M312 contract already says exact_valid825_baseline=true. Post-run code checks valid825=true and accuracy_promoted=false but not paired_baseline=null or system/ppa/headline=false.
findings.impact: A contract intent can be mistaken for completed evidence, and a forged receipt can carry contradictory claims into the baseline seal.
findings.required_fix: Keep pre-run evidence false and require the complete exact-baseline admission tuple before writing the launch receipt.

findings.title: The enabled equals-form duplicate fails only in the downstream generic parser
findings.evidence: M313 accepts an extra --enabled-operator-indices=value at its outer check; after deleting the exact pair the generic M284 parser rejects the leftover option as unknown.
findings.impact: The selected set cannot be changed by this form, but the dedicated launcher is not the component providing the promised rejection.
findings.required_fix: Normalize and reject the duplicate before importing the wrapper.

findings.title: Bound files are not all rehashed at the final seal boundary
findings.evidence: M313 checks inputs at different times and M312 only rechecks launcher source immediately before success.
findings.impact: A concurrent replacement between validation and sealing is not explicitly detected.
findings.required_fix: Snapshot canonical paths and hashes, then rehash every bound input and output immediately before committing the launch receipt and seal.

next_action: Do not start M312. Repair the two root P0s and the manifest/nested-identity boundary, regenerate the M312 contract because launcher SHA will change, and request a new preflight. Only after a sealed repaired baseline may M313's exact-SHA candidate contract be generated and independently reviewed.
